output.best_reason: Version B has the most natural facts-in-motion: Girard explains the repeater's chimes in his own trade terms (hours, quarters, minutes), so the clue lands as expertise rather than a recited timestamp. Its opening frames the stakes (Aurèle is dead, everyone is being asked) and gives Girard a distinct, haggling merchant voice. The closing instruction to stay in the house adds pressure. Version D is close behind, with a strong, guarded voice and a sharp closing line ("I have never killed one. Write that down if you must."), but it leans on repeated disclaimers about what he did not see, which slows it. Version C has vivid personal texture, though its watch-timestamps are more heavily stacked and its voice occasionally slips into generic colloquialism. Version A is the most list-like: its answers repeat "by my watch" in nearly every line and read as a recited timeline, with the least distinct voice.
